Canonicalization + identity agreement across Langsys SDKs. AUTHORED in langsys-js-typescript, not vendored from another lane.
purpose: Proof that the SDKs mint the SAME custom_id for the same content, covering the canonicalization rules added in the TOK batch: U+00A0 collapse, attribute values collapsing internal whitespace like text nodes, and the fixed twenty-seven translatable attributes in their fixed order.
how_to_row_against_it: Tokenize the html field, compare to expected_tokens, then hash (category, tokens) and compare to expected_custom_id. Compare CODEPOINTS, not display strings: several cases differ only by U+00A0 or U+2028, which render identically to a space — the html_codepoints and expected_tokens_codepoints fields exist so a mismatch is readable instead of looking like two identical strings with two different hashes.
expected_is: What langsys-js-typescript produces, which matches the spec at blob 318b594173c7470fbcfcf1eaec19ff9e62bec517 for every row here. Where a lane diverges, the divergence field names which lane and why. It is not an invitation to change the expectation.

measured_at.langsys2 (server): NO MINTER EXISTS. Searched by hashing call and by canonical-serialization signature, with the same searches positive-controlled against langsys-php-sdk (4 hits there, 0 here). The backend stores ids clients send; it does not compute them.

cases.why: noscript IS prose and must be harvested (TOK-1)
cases.divergence: TOK-1 reversed and now EXCLUDES noscript, so this SDK contributes no token. PHP still harvests it: libxml2 has no scripting flag and parses the children as elements. Excluding it is what makes the two parser models agree, so this row should stop diverging once PHP adopts the reversal.

PHP does not collapse U+2028/U+2029 either. Same root cause as the NBSP rows. Worth noting the consequence for the three-flag json_encode work: in a DOM-tokenized path these never reach the serializer on the JS side because they collapse to spaces first, so the flags matter for a caller hashing its own token array, not for tokenized content.
